title_candidates: OpenAI's education plugins start with school-controlled access
summary: OpenAI added separate ChatGPT Work and Codex plugins for K-12 teachers, college educators, and students inside managed education workspaces.

primary_source.title: New ways to learn and teach with ChatGPT Work and Codex
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: OpenAI introduced three education plugins: one for K-12 teachers, one for college educators, and one for college students.
The plugins package role-specific instructions, skills, connected apps, and common workflows so users need less prompt setup.
The K-12 plugin can help create differentiated resources, interactive visuals, and standards-aligned materials while educators retain control over pedagogy, grading, and agent actions.
The college educator plugin can work with approved course materials, calendars, documents, and tools to produce syllabi, assessments, teaching sites, and LMS-ready content.
The college student plugin can turn selected course sources into guided tutoring, quizzes, flashcards, study guides, and interactive explanations.
Access is limited to ChatGPT Edu and ChatGPT for Teachers district deployments, where institutions control available tools and permissions.

quote_candidates.text: AI should support learning, not shortcut it, and the best learning experiences keep educators and students in control.

supporting_sources.title: Plugins in ChatGPT and Codex
key_facts: Users can inspect a plugin's included apps, connection requirements, terms, and privacy policy before connecting it.
Workspace administrators can limit plugins and their apps by role, data source, read or write actions, approval requirements, and sync boundaries.
A plugin can be invoked in ChatGPT with an at-mention or the plus menu, and in supported Codex task views through Sources and Use plugins.

supporting_sources.title: ChatGPT for Teachers
key_facts: ChatGPT for Teachers is designed for verified staff at accredited U.S. K-12 schools and districts, but the education plugins require a district deployment rather than an individual account alone.

prerequisites: Access to a managed ChatGPT Edu or ChatGPT for Teachers district workspace
The matching education plugin enabled by your workspace administrator
A fictional or public learning objective with no student records

steps.instruction: Open the ChatGPT plugin directory while signed into your education workspace and search for the K-12 Educator, College Educator, or College Student plugin. Stop and ask your administrator if it is absent or disabled.

Open the listing and review its included apps, requested permissions, terms, and privacy policy. Connect only an institution-approved app, and keep the first test read-only and limited to non-sensitive material.

Invoke the plugin with an at-mention or the plus menu, then give it a fictional objective such as comparing three quarters with five eighths. Ask for three exit-ticket questions, an answer key, and the source concept behind each answer.
Solve every question independently and check each answer and claimed standard against the original material. Revise or discard anything unsupported.
Keep the result private until an educator approves it. Do not publish, grade, message students, or connect private records during this first test.

risk_flags: The plugins are not broadly available to individual consumer accounts; the article must state that access requires a managed education deployment.
Signal already covered generic role plugins and educator training; keep this article focused on the three education-specific workflows and institution-managed controls.
The guide uses fictional material, read-only permissions, independent verification, and an explicit stop before real student use.
